# Weight {#sec-dd-weight}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$weight
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
```

## Overview

The revenue weight is the vehicle's maximum permitted gross weight in
kilograms, as the DVLA records it. It matters most for goods vehicles and
buses, which are classed by weight.

- **`revenue_weight`** is the harmonised weight: the DVLA value where the VES
  record describes this vehicle, otherwise the most common value among
  vehicles of the same make, model, birth year, fuel and engine size, and
  failing that of the same make, model, birth year and fuel.
- **`revenue_weight_src`** says which (`dvla`, `variant` or
  `model_year_fuel`).
- **`revenueWeight_DVLA`** is the value as supplied.

The backfill is described in the methodology,
[section 5.6](../../reports/methodology.md#other-attributes).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-weight
#| tbl-cap: "Weight columns."
dict_table("weight")
```

## Coverage

The weight is the least complete of the DVLA attributes. The DVLA records it
for only `r cov_pct(cs, "revenueWeight_DVLA")` of vehicles, even though a VES
record was found for far more, and most of those with a weight were first used
since 2010 (@fig-dd-weight). The backfill raises coverage to
`r cov_pct(cs, "revenue_weight")`, but only to
`r cov_pct(cs, "revenue_weight", "Before 2000")` for vehicles first used before
2000, as few similar vehicles of that age have a recorded weight to copy.

Because most values are filled rather than recorded, check results that
depend on weight against the recorded values only
(`revenue_weight_src = 'dvla'`; @sec-pitfalls).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-weight-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-weight
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles with a revenue weight, as supplied by the DVLA and harmonised, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 2.6
coverage_plot(c("revenueWeight_DVLA", "revenue_weight"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from
1990. Numeric columns show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper
quartile (Q3) and maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each
value, with the less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing
values as *Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("weight"))
```
